title: Arc Welding and Fire Prevention
summary: An arc welder is safe when it is inspected and used right, but misuse leads to fire, explosion, and eye burns. This talk covers fire control, grounding, and protection while welding.
talking_points: Inspect the arc welder before you strike an arc. Ground the welder case and read the warning labels and manual.
Clear all fire hazards - oil, grease, flammables, and loose metal shavings - from at least 35 feet around the work area.
Insulate your body from the metal you are welding. Wear dry gloves in good condition, long sleeves, long pants, and the right footwear.
Never strike an arc without proper eye protection in place.
Keep the right fire extinguisher within reach. Use a combination Class A, B, C extinguisher for most welding. For magnesium fires use Class D, or smother with dry sand or magnesium foundry flux.
Post a fire watcher when you weld or cut near combustible material or anything closer than 35 feet to the work.
site_hazards_to_check: Combustible material, flammable liquids, or gas cylinders within 35 feet of the arc
Magnesium shavings, cuttings, or other reactive metals on the floor
Missing, wrong-class, or discharged fire extinguisher
Ungrounded welder case or damaged leads and cables
Damaged, wet, or oily gloves and clothing
discussion_questions: What flammable materials are in our work area today, and how will we move or shield them?
Which class of fire extinguisher is staged here, and is it the right one for this job?
Who is the fire watcher, and how long do they stay after we stop welding?

flags: OSHA mapping and tolerances verified accurate: 29 CFR 1926.351 (arc welding and cutting - incl. grounding of the welder case) and 1926.352 (fire prevention). The 35 ft clearance for combustible material and flammables (1926.352(a)) and the fire-watch requirement (1926.352(d)-(e)) are stated correctly and consistently. Class A:B:C extinguisher for general welding, Class D or dry sand / foundry flux for magnesium fires, insulate the body from the work, and no arc without eye protection - all accurate.
Non-blocking enhancement: consider adding 29 CFR 1926.353 (ventilation and protection in welding/cutting/heating) and 1926.102 for the eye-protection point.
